info.title: yarr
info.description: HTTP API of yarr, a self-hostable RSS/Atom/JSON feed aggregator. This document covers the JSON API served under /api, OPML import/export, the reader-view page-crawl endpoint, and the health check. It does NOT cover the Fever-compatible API served under /fever/ (a separate third-party-compatible surface), the JSON-RPC Model Context Protocol endpoint at POST /mcp (see doc/mcp.md) or the browser/UI surfaces (/, /static/*, /manifest.json, /sw.js, /logout). When yarr is started with --auth (or --auth-file), every endpoint documented here except GET /up and GET /v1/openapi.json requires a valid `auth` session cookie, obtained by signing in through the HTML login form; requests without it receive a redirect/401 from the auth middleware rather than reaching these handlers. Response bodies and status codes below describe the handlers' actual behavior, including cases where the code returns 200 on what looks like a failure, or falls back to an empty 200 body because a route has no explicit handling for a given HTTP method.

get.description: Reports whether the process is able to serve traffic. Does no I/O and does not touch the database, so it cannot detect a broken database connection. Always public, even when --auth is configured (it is listed in the auth middleware's Public paths). Any HTTP method reaches this handler (the router does not restrict by method), and it always runs the same GET-shaped logic.

200.description: Process is ready to serve traffic.

503.description: Process is starting up or shutting down.

get.description: Serves this hand-written OpenAPI 3.1 document describing yarr's API. Intended to be public (not gated by --auth) so external tooling (e.g. Outpost's Hermes SKILL.md generator) can fetch it without credentials; whether it is actually reachable without auth depends on it being added to the auth middleware's Public path list at the call site in routes.go.

200.description: The OpenAPI document.

get.summary: Worker status and per-feed unread/starred counts
get.description: The handler does not check the request method; any HTTP method reaches this same logic and returns 200.

200.description: Current refresh status and feed stats.

running.description: True while the background feed-refresh worker has feeds pending.

200.description: All folders, ordered by title (case-insensitive).

201.description: Folder created (or, if a folder with the same title already exists, its title is re-set and its id is returned).

400.description: Malformed JSON body, or `title` missing/empty. A missing/empty title returns a JSON body `{"error": "Folder title missing."}`; a JSON decode failure returns an empty body.

405.description: Method other than GET or POST.

put.summary: Rename a folder and/or toggle its expanded state
put.description: Both fields are optional; whichever are present in the body are applied. Neither field being present is a no-op that still returns 200.

200.description: Updated (empty body).

400.description: `id` is not an integer, or the JSON body is malformed.

delete.description: Feeds inside the folder are not deleted; see the `feeds` table's foreign key behavior in src/storage.

204.description: Deleted (empty body). Returned even if no folder with this id existed.

200.description: All feeds, ordered by title (case-insensitive). `icon` is never populated by this listing query (only `has_icon` is); fetch /api/feeds/{id}/icon for the actual icon bytes.

post.summary: Subscribe to a feed (or discover candidate feeds at a URL)
post.description: Given a URL, tries to parse it directly as a feed; if that fails, scrapes the page for <link> feed autodiscovery tags. Always responds 200, even when nothing is found or the URL is unreachable — the outcome is communicated only via the `status` field in the body.

200.description: One of three shapes depending on `status`: `notfound` (URL unreachable or no feed/links found), `multiple` (the page links to more than one feed — `choice` lists the candidates), or `success` (a feed was created and its items fetched — `feed` is the new Feed).

post.summary: Trigger a background refresh of all feeds
post.description: Enqueues a refresh and returns immediately; refreshing happens asynchronously in the worker.

200.description: Refresh triggered (empty body).

get.description: Only feeds that currently have a recorded error are present.

200.description: Map of feed id (as a string, since JSON object keys are always strings) to the last error message for that feed.

get.description: The handler does not check the request method; any HTTP method reaches this same logic. Response is cached in-process (keyed by feed id) after the first request. Supports conditional requests via If-None-Match.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: ETag (md5 of the icon bytes, truncated to 16 hex chars) from a previous response.

200.description: Icon bytes. Content-Type is sniffed from the bytes via http.DetectContentType.

304.description: If-None-Match matched the current icon's ETag.

404.description: Feed does not exist, or has no icon.

put.summary: Update a feed's title, folder, and/or feed URL
put.description: The request body is decoded into a generic JSON object rather than a fixed struct; only the keys `title` (string), `folder_id` (number or null), and `feed_link` (string) are recognized, and each is applied independently only if present and of the expected JSON type — wrong-typed values for a recognized key are silently ignored rather than rejected. Unrecognized keys are ignored.

200.description: Updated (empty body).

400.description: `id` is not an integer, no feed with that id exists, or the JSON body is malformed.

405.description: Method other than PUT or DELETE.
Method other than PUT or DELETE.

get.description: Page size is fixed at 20 and is not configurable by the client. `after` is a cursor: it names an existing item id, and the response continues strictly before/after that item's (date, id) position in the requested sort order — it is not a byte/row offset. Items with an empty title have one synthesized from the first 140 characters of their (HTML-stripped) content.

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Restrict to feeds in this folder.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Id of an item to page from; results continue after its position in the current sort order.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by status. Note: an unrecognized value is not rejected — storage.StatusValues[status] returns the zero value (unread) for any string it doesn't recognize, so a typo silently filters for unread items.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Full-text search (SQLite FTS `search` table) over title/content, tokenized on whitespace with a trailing-wildcard prefix match on each term.

parameters.name: oldest_first
parameters.description: Sort ascending by date when exactly the string "true"; any other value (including absent) sorts newest-first. Not a boolean-typed query param — compared as a literal string.

200.description: A page of items plus a has_more flag.

list.description: Each item's `content` field is the raw, unsanitized content (unlike GET /api/items/{id}, this list endpoint does not run it through the HTML sanitizer).

put.description: Marks every item matching the filter as read, except items that are starred (starred items are never auto-marked read by this endpoint). With no filter parameters, this marks every non-starred item in the database as read.

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Restrict to feeds in this folder.

200.description: Marked (empty body).

get.description: Content and media-link descriptions are HTML-sanitized before being returned, and a relative `link` is resolved to an absolute URL against the parent feed's link. Note: if the item does not exist, the handler returns 400 Bad Request, not 404.

200.description: The item.

400.description: `id` is not an integer, or no item with that id exists.

200.description: Updated (empty body). A body with `status` omitted is a no-op that still returns 200.

400.description: `id` is not an integer, or the JSON body is malformed.

405.description: Method other than GET or PUT.

post.description: Requires instapaper_username and instapaper_password to already be set via PUT /api/settings. On success, marks the item's `instapaper_saved` true and its status `read`, then returns the updated item.

200.description: Saved to Instapaper. Returns the item as it stands after being updated (instapaper_saved=true, status=read).

400.description: `id` is not an integer, or Instapaper credentials are not configured.

404.description: No item with that id exists.

502.description: The request to Instapaper's API failed or was rejected.

get.description: Returns the defaults merged with any stored overrides. The exact key set is fixed (see Settings schema) but the endpoint has no declared response type in the code — it is a plain map[string]interface{}, so `additionalProperties` is intentionally left open here.

200.description: Current settings.

put.description: Body is a map of setting key to new value. Keys not present in the fixed default-settings set are silently ignored (not rejected). Setting `refresh_rate` also live-updates the worker's refresh ticker.

200.description: Updated (empty body).

400.description: Malformed JSON body, or the update failed to persist.

post.summary: Import subscriptions from an OPML file
post.description: multipart/form-data with the OPML file in a field named `opml`. Imported feeds are not fetched inline; the handler kicks off favicon discovery and a full feed refresh in the background and returns immediately. Note: if the `opml` form field/file is missing or unreadable, the handler logs the error and returns without writing any status, which falls through to an implicit 200 with an empty body — the same as success.

200.description: Import kicked off (or the form field was missing/unreadable — see description).

400.description: The uploaded file could not be parsed as OPML.

get.description: Method is not checked in an else-branch, but only GET has any handling; other methods fall through to an implicit 200 with an empty body.

200.description: OPML XML document, served as an attachment (Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="subscriptions.opml").

get.summary: Fetch a URL server-side and extract readable article content
get.description: Used by the UI's reader view. Does not check the request method — any HTTP method reaches this logic. If the URL is a recognized video page (YouTube/Vimeo), returns a sanitized <iframe> embed instead of crawling. Requests targeting an internal/private IP are refused, but silently: the handler logs a warning server-side and returns without writing any response status or body, which the client sees as 200 with an empty body. If article extraction fails, the error is NOT surfaced as an HTTP error — the handler still returns 200, with `content` set to the string "error: <message>".

200.description: Extracted (sanitized) HTML content, a video-embed iframe, an "error: ..." content string on extraction failure, or an empty body if the URL was refused as internal (see description).

400.description: The URL could not be fetched.

cookieAuth.name: auth
cookieAuth.description: Set by the HTML login form when yarr is started with --auth or --auth-file. Value is "<username>:<hmac>"; validity is checked by src/server/auth. Only present/enforced when yarr was started with auth configured.

MediaLink.description: An enclosure/media link extracted from a feed item (podcast audio, images, etc).

type.description: MIME type, as declared by the feed.

Item.description: A feed entry, from src/storage/item.go Item.

content.description: HTML. Omitted from the JSON body entirely when empty (omitempty).

status.description: Stored internally as an integer (0/1/2) but marshaled to/from these string names.

Feed.description: A subscribed feed, from src/storage/feed.go Feed.

icon.description: Raw icon bytes, base64-encoded by Go's JSON marshaler. Only present when the query that produced this Feed selected it (GET /api/feeds/{id} does; GET /api/feeds does not); omitted from the JSON body when nil (omitempty).

FeedSource.description: A candidate feed discovered on a page, from src/worker/crawler.go FeedSource.

FolderUpdateForm.description: All fields optional; only the fields present are applied.

url.description: A feed URL, or a page URL to autodiscover feed(s) on.

Settings.description: From src/storage/settings.go settingsDefaults(); GET /api/settings returns this shape merged with any stored overrides, so additional keys should not appear but the type itself is a plain map with no server-side schema enforcement.

refresh_rate.description: Seconds between automatic refreshes; 0 disables auto-refresh.
